entityDescription:
Eni is an energy company that integrates technology and sustainability in all its business areas, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals set out by the UN in 2015. We are engaged in the exploration, production, refining and sale of oil, gas, electricity and chemicals. Our entire value and production chain is founded upon the single goal of achieving full decarbonization by providing accessible and clean energy to all. As the world continues to demand more energy, we are responding with a mix of natural gas and renewables, pursuing a path that will ensure the gradual and economically sustainable replacement of high-carbon sources with cleaner alternatives. These clearly defined policies, which apply around the world and successfully attract investment, allow us to focus on what we do best: bringing our skills and expertise to the transition towards low-carbon sources such as renewable energy and natural gas. Eni is committed to an energy transition that is socially fair and that, through tangible solutions, preserves the environment and provides everyone with access to the energy they need.
Eni pillars are: sustainability, people and technological innovation.
Sustainability
is critical for long-lasting results and strengthening the company’s reputation and business performance. Eni promotes a model of cooperation in the 66 Countries where we are active, providing them with tangible support which allows us to develop energy sources and infrastructures while supporting improvements across society, education, health and culture.
People are our most important asset. All our achievements are a result of the skill and passion that Eni’s 31,321 people bring to everything they do. This is why we ensure that our employees are able to grow through continuous professional development in an environment that cares about their quality of life – both within the company and beyond.
Technological innovation is a key driver for our company. Every day we explore new paths, pursue efficiency in all our activities and make the most of our financial and energy resources, as well as our wealth of expertise.

entityDescription:
SES is a state institution under supervision of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia. SES was established on 1st of January 2005 integrating former State Environmental Inspectorate, 8 Regional Environmental Boards and Marine Environmental Board. Since 1st of July 2009 in the course of reorganization, the Radiation Safety Centre was joined with SES and become the State Environmental Service Radiation Safety Centre of the Republic of Latvia. The goal of SES is to ensure the compliance of implementation of legislation framework in the area of the environment and natural resources protection, and control on radiation and nuclear safety.
Functions of the State Environmental Service: according to the procedure provided in the laws and regulations regulating the protection of the environment to carry out the state control of the environment protection and natural resources use in the territory of Latvia, continental shelf, economic zones of the Baltic Sea and Rīga Gulf, territorial waters and inland waters; according to the procedure provided in the laws and regulations concerning fishing to provide the control of the fishing carried out by the Latvia’s fishing vessels in the waters of the European Union member states, of states which are not member states of the European Union and in the high seas; according to the procedure provided in the laws and regulations concerning radiation safety and nuclear safety to provide supervision and control on issues concerning radiation safety and nuclear safety.

Tensorflight was founded in 2016 by Zbigniew Wojna and Robert Kozikowski. Zbigniew is a co-author of one of the publication tables in the field of computer creation of the last few years, contains the best classification model in the world, which is the first downloaded human accuracy. Robert is still an ex googler and a top researcher in Big Data. Zbigniew also has become the winner of SpaceNet 6 in June 2020.
The key specialization of the company is an innovation consisting in the creation of computers and the use of artificial intelligence, which can analyze many types of images and build data available to them around the world. The Tensorflight website contains, first and foremost, information about our solution, and photos are automatically analyzed using artificial intelligence algorithms that provide information on a set of types, building size. Although we are not limited to them, there is a need for detection with supported / aerial / Streetview images of objects, or analysis of entire applications, we are certainly responsible and reliable partners. We are happy to know all the needs and technological problems for solutions in the industry. Perhaps some of them will be able to be solved by adapting our solutions.
Our solution applies Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision. Given an address or coordinates of the property, our algorithms locate the building at that address, extract satellite, aerial and street view imagery of the property and then automatically analyze the images, and returning in less than 15 seconds the unique information (as a report structure) about the building such as footprint, square footage, construction type, number of stories, roof pitch, roof geometry, roof material, object length, object width, occupancy type, information on solar panels, distance from the nearest tree and distance from neighboring objects. In addition, we could adapt the use of our platform so that system will allow the risk engineer to enter all necessary parameters mention in this challenge description.
The innovation is based on Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence, capable of analyzing multiple image types and building a database of all buildings around the globe. The following information is provided to insurance and reinsurance companies. Our key features are Construction – the most basic element of the building. It means the material types from which the building is made of. Many insurers classify buildings into categories based on their construction type using a system developed by the Insurance Services Office (ISO). This system includes six classes. Each classification reflects both the building materials used (such as wood or concrete) and the combustibility of these materials. Occupancy -This term means the purpose for which the property is used. Examples are the retail food market, furniture manufacturing, and apartments. Protection- Protection means the methods used to safeguard a building from fire. It includes both public and private protection. Exposure: It refers to external hazards that exist largely due to the building's location. Some hazards are natural. A building located in a breezy area may be subject to damage by high winds. Other natural hazards include sinkholes, hail, lightning, and heavy snow. Natural hazards can vary widely from one location to another. The intention of Tensorflight’s team is to build an ecosystem that addresses the needs of insurance companies in terms of risk evaluation, which according to sources are construction, occupancy, protection, and exposure.

Agricultural University – Plovdiv 
The Agricultural University of Plovdiv was established in 1945. It is the only specialized state university in Bulgaria in the area of agricultural and related sciences, enjoying national, European and international prestige. In 2019 it was granted an institutional accreditation with a grade of 9.61 on the ten-point scale, which places our educational institution among the TOP THREE universities in Bulgaria.
University Mission:To provide high quality training, guaranteeing student knowledge, entrepreneurial skills, self-confidence for successful transition to the Bulgarian and European labour market; To train experts who are able to provide healthy and safe food, feed and biofuels, complying to the high requirements of the European standards through the use of innovative practices under the conditions of the information society. To conduct fundamental and applied research studies, oriented towards rapid implementation in practice for adequate integration of the sector into European agriculture. To build a responsible attitude towards farming as a provider of public services, including those related to climate change. To preserve the love of the Bulgarians of the land, the thirst for knowledge and the traditions of the higher agricultural education, giving increasing importance to values and ethical public understanding for preserving traditional products and production technologies.
The major structural units are the four faculties (Faculty of Agronomy, Faculty of Horticulture with Viticulture, Faculty of Plant Protection and Agroecology, Faculty of Economics). Training is provided for acquiring the Bachelor’s and Master’s degree in eight professional fields. 27 doctoral programmes are also available. 
AU is active in the international education scene through Erasmus+ cooperation with foreign universities for project implementation and exchange of students and teachers, improvement of curricula and study programmes, double and joint degrees within Europe, and with Central Asia and Africa. 
Major aspects in international activities:
Bilateral cooperation with foreign universities for exchange of experience, improvement of curricula and study programmes, double and joint degrees;
Participation in international educational and research projects on unmanned and digital technologies in agriculture;
Enlarging Еразъм+ bilateral agreements in geographical coverage;
In the frames of Erasmus+ KA 103 and KA 107 the AUP has over 90 Partners offering staff mobility and student mobility for training and internships.
Over 50 new Memoranda of Understanding and Framework agreements have been signed in the last year, enlarging partnership with countries from new geographical areas, such as Uzbekistan, China, South Africa, Ukraine, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan.
The research policy. The University addresses the current and future technologies in agronomy, plant protection, agroecology, environment safety, marketing and management of agri-food holdings, agri-food quality and safety, recycling, etc. Extensive experimental fields (i.e. vineyards, horticulture and animal husbandry) allow for integrated applied research in priority areas such as food and nutrition security, sustainable agriculture and forestry, environmental quality and food safety, responses to climate change, environment and resource efficiency.

The Industrial Systems Institute (ISI)is a leading R&D institute of excellence conducting basic research and exploratory development on Information and communications technology (ICT) for the Greek and European industry established in Patras in 1998. 

From the time of its inauguration, the focus of ISI has been on edge technologies for industrial operations/enterprise environments, and prime concern towards innovation and the growth in competitiveness of the Greek industry. General goal of ISI has from the outset been to conduct applied research leading the development of industrial applications and products, as well as the provision of advanced industrial services. LEVITY is a lean NewSpace StartUp from Aachen, Germany. Recently established out of a funded university project, LEVITY aims to lower the barriers for the NewSpace participants and newcomers to space. LEVITY’s vision is to establish a NewSpace infrastructure for Earth and Moon up to Deep Space, providing a universal, plug-and-play, flexible, low-thrust, small satellite platform relying on microlaunchers. LEVITY concentrates on developing and integrating satellite components and systems, outsourcing manufacturing completely. 
Next to the overall company vision, LEVITY will commercialize its Spin-Off Products, among them the wireless module SKITH - Skip The Harness. In cooperation with the University of Würzburg and Prof. Sergio Montenegro, this award-winning technology allows wireless communication within systems, greatly reducing failure points and reducing harness. LEVITY foresees to implement the technology within its own products as well as commercially manufacture and distribute it for both space and non-space applications.

Created in 1992, LEPAC is a private, independent think tank, based in France, specialised in geopolitics and future studies, and praised for its early and extensive work on global transition, and its thirty-year expertise in mapping and data visualisation. 

By relying on a multidisciplinary network of researchers and combining extensive data analysis and field missions, LEPAC offers to enlighten policies and decisions whether through private consultancies, books, keynotes speeches, TV programs, seminars or educational publications. Based on a transversal and systemic approach to international issues, it breaks down the barriers of knowledge, connects the dots between events and data, deciphers complex problems, sheds light on the challenges and mechanisms of transition, and renders them in a trusted educational approach. 

From 1992 to 2018, LEPAC produced all the visual and editorial content for the famous geopolitical educational TV program named *Le Dessous des Cartes* or *Mit offenen Karten*, aired on the bilingual French-German channel Arte. Since 1992, LEPAC also has sold over 450,000 copies of the different books it has edited and published, including those resulting from the research program denoted *The World’s Future*, which seeks to explore and define the global challenges the world will face by 2050.

entityDescription:
The Catalonia Institute for Energy Research (IREC) is a publicly funded institution with a staff of approximately 120 people created in 2008 based in Barcelona and Tarragona that conducts research and promotes innovation over a wide range of disciplines within the science and technology energy field. IREC contributes to sustainability via development of new technological solutions, promotion of scientific and technological know-how related to sustainable energy and its efficient use as well transfer of solution and expertise to market actors and policymakers. IREC has large expertise and skills in research and industrial projects, with an annual turnover of about 10M�. IREC belongs to the CERCA and TECNIO networks of research and technologic centers of the Generalitat of Catalunya covering the two objectives of its mission: i) technological development that promotes technology transfer and ii) position as an international reference research center focused on disruptive energy results.
Activities and objectives of IREC are organized in 5 main axes covering the R&D&I energy area: Renewable energy sources, Circular economy technologies, Smart energy management and systems, Energy systems analytics, and Energy Storage. IREC is structured in 2 large areas: 
· Energy Efficiency: Systems, Buildings and Communities (ECOS).Its focuses on energy efficiency in systems, buildings and communities and offshore wind energy. In particular, ECOS uses industry-oriented experimental development platforms for extensive validation of technologies and integration of energy systems prior certification or commercialization. Expertise and topics include: nearly Zero Energy Buildings (nZEB), flexible buildings, renewable energy sources integration, onshore and offshore wind farms, smart grids and micro-grids, smart sensing, integration of smart mobility, green IT, energy economics and regulations, energy systems analytics.
· Advanced Materials for Energy (M2E). This area focuses on energy storage, either by electrochemical or chemical technologies as well as new concepts regarding batteries and superconductors. Expertise and topics include: functional nanomaterials, catalysis, new materials for photovoltaic energy, nanoionics and fuel cells (e.g., hydrogen), energy storage and harvesters, carbon capture use and sequestration (CCUS)
Actions include national and international projects as well as direct cooperation with leading industrial partners and governmental authorities. International projects include those from the International Energy Agency (IEA) where we act as Operating Agent in some efforts (e.g., Task 28), projects funded by the European Commission (e.g., FP7 and H2020) as well as bilateral collaborations with international entities (e.g., Qatar). In addition, IREC belongs to relevant national and international platforms, including: Energy Materials Industrial Research Initiative-EMIRI (https://emiri.eu/), Fuel Cells and Hydrogen Joint Undertaking-FCH JU (http://www.fch-ju.eu/), the Spanish CO2 technology platform-PTECO2 (http://www.pteco2.es/) and several Joint Programs of the European Energy Research Alliance (EERA, www.eera-set.eu) namely on Smart Grids, on Energy Systems Integration, and on Economic Environmental and Social impact. IREC is full member of the KIC InnoEnergy to promote the energy innovation in Europe and also leads the Energy for Society research network (XRE4S) and the RIS3CAT Energy Community in order to promote the transformation and competitiveness of the energy sector in Catalonia. Finally, IREC leads the bFUS program for the development of technology and the industrial sector in nuclear fusion.

iCOMAT’s Rapid Tow Shearing (RTS) is the world’s first automated composites manufacturing process that can place carbon fibre tapes along curved paths without generating defects. Our unique defect-free fibre steering capability enables ultra-lightweight composite structures beyond the limit of the conventional straight-fibre designs and complex geometry which is not manufacturable using current automated manufacturing technologies.

entityDescription:
The University of Girona (UdG), located in the city of Girona, has been part of the Catalan public university system since 1992. With deep roots in Catalonia and its culture, the UdG is strongly committed to the universal missions of universities. It plays a pivotal role as a key driver of economic and social progress in the region. The UdG is devoted to excellence in both teaching and research, and it seeks to contribute to society’s progress and development through the creation, dissemination, transference, and knowledge review related to Sciences, Technology, Humanities, and Arts. Over 100 research groups, distributed in 24 departments and 12 research institutes, comprise the University’s rich and varied investigation landscape. A considerable part of this research is conducted in international contexts, where the UdG has gained wide experience in the management and coordination of international and European grants.

Infrastructure and Academic Capacity: UdG operates across 3 campuses, with 9 faculties and schools, 6 affiliated centers,1 Research and Innovation Park,12 research institutes, and 3 CERCA-affiliated institutes. It supports a vibrant community of over 15,500 students,+1600 researchers and faculty members, and +600 administrative and management staff. The university offers 49 undergraduate degrees,29 official master's programs, 14 doctoral programs, and multiple international double degrees. 
With +200 active research projects - including31 Horizon Europe projects,56 SGR-recognized research groups,7 TECNIO-certified groups,4 European patents, and7 technological spin-offs, UdG stands out for its innovation and knowledge transfer capabilities. Its scientific output during 2024-2025 included 1,083 ISI-indexed articles,249 book chapters, and 33 research books.
UdG actively participates in European and international projects, with a strong focus on interdisciplinarity,cross-border cooperation, andglobal talent development. UdG is a member of the ACROSS European University Alliance, recognized by the European Commission, and actively contributes to cross-border knowledge sharing and regional development. Its UdG2030 strategy reinforces its commitment to the SDGs,digital transformation, gender equality, and climate resilience. The university leads initiatives inAI ethics, sustainable water management,digital transformation, and health innovation, including two strategic chairs funded by Next Generation EU: one in AI for diabetes and another in cybersecurity for water system.
